claims.text: A neural-network machine-learning potential trained on ab initio liquid and solid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to standard EAM references.
The proposed machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Training configurations that include both liquid and solid atomic environments provides adequate coverage for the relevant high-entropy-alloy phase space.
Atomic-configuration diversity is highest near the melting point.
Traditional EAM potentials have limitations for high-entropy alloys near their melting points.
Improved representation of disordered liquid local environments produces better reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved representation of short-range ordering near melting produces better reference–target phase-space overlap.
A comprehensive ab initio training set enables the machine-learning potential to capture subtle interatomic interactions.
A comprehensive ab initio training set enables the machine-learning potential to capture structural fluctuations in both phases.
Capturing subtle interatomic interactions and structural fluctuations leads to a smoother and more continuous thermodynamic-integration path than standard EAM references provide.
The intervention is expected to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by roughly 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The approach is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys at or near their high melting temperatures.
EAM potentials can adequately capture configuration space in elemental systems or simpler binary alloys.
The machine-learning intervention may provide negligible improvement in elemental systems or simpler binary alloys.
